definition: In psychological assessment, an inventory is a structured measure used to evaluate a set of symptoms or traits. In this packet, it refers to a validated self-report measure for depressive symptoms.

reasons: The packet supports only a specific instrument, the Quick Inventory of Depressive Symptomatology (QIDS), as a validated measure of depressive symptoms; it does not support a general definition of an "inventory" as a structured measure of symptoms or traits.

The wording "In this packet, it refers to a validated self-report measure for depressive symptoms" overgeneralizes from the specific QIDS description and does not establish the broader term sense requested.
The packet does not support the general claim that, in psychological assessment, an “inventory” is broadly “a structured measure used to evaluate a set of symptoms or traits.”

While the packet supports that the Quick Inventory of Depressive Symptomatology (QIDS) is a “validated measure” of depressive symptoms, it does not justify the broader dictionary-style definition of “inventory” given in the first sentence.

The statement that “in this packet, it refers to a validated self-report measure for depressive symptoms” is only partially supported: the packet calls QIDS validated and describes DSM-IV coverage, but does not explicitly state “self-report” in the provided text (it mentions a “self-reported version” only for the Japanese translation).
